library_preparation_preflight.summary: onnxruntime is self-contained (bundled multi-platform natives, zero transitive deps, no server component); no dependency/Docker setup needed, but meaningful tests need an embedded minimal ONNX model since the Java API has no model-builder classes.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: To exercise OrtEnvironment.createSession(...)/OrtSession.run(...) meaningfully, tests need an actual .onnx model (binary protobuf graph). The onnxruntime Java jar only exposes inference APIs, not a model builder, and there is no network access during generation/test runs to download one. Embed a tiny valid ONNX model as raw bytes (a trivial single-node graph, e.g. Identity or Add, is only ~100-200 bytes) directly in test source or as a checked-in test resource, rather than assuming a model can be fetched or built on the fly. Coverage of OrtEnvironment lifecycle, SessionOptions configuration, OnnxTensor creation from Java arrays, and exception types does not require a model and can be tested independently.
risks: JDK 24+ (JEP 472) is tightening JNI native-access restrictions; verify locally whether JDK 25 requires --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED for this JNI-based library or still only warns.

Native library extraction writes to java.io.tmpdir and loads via System.load(); if the native-image test environment ever mounts /tmp noexec, loading would fail silently with an UnsatisfiedLinkError — unlikely on standard CI runners but worth confirming during nativeTestCompile/test.
This decision covers the CPU onnxruntime artifact only; the separate onnxruntime_gpu artifact (CUDA/cuDNN) is out of scope and would need materially different setup if ever requested.
